title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Unity fundamentals, installation, and the editor interface!

questions.question: Unity is a _________ 3D development platform.
questions.explanation: Unity is a real-time engine, meaning it renders graphics instantly as you interact.

questions.question: Which application is used to manage Unity installations and projects?
questions.explanation: Unity Hub is the launcher that handles multiple Editor versions and projects.

questions.question: What is the primary scripting language for Unity?
questions.explanation: C# (pronounced C-sharp) is the main language used for Unity scripting.

questions.question: Which template is best for a beginner starting a standard 3D game?
questions.explanation: 3D Core provides the simplest setup without advanced rendering pipelines.

questions.question: Where should you place all your game assets (scripts, textures, models)?
questions.explanation: The Assets folder is the root for all user-created or imported content.

questions.question: Which window shows the properties of the currently selected object?
questions.explanation: The Inspector displays all components and values attached to the selected GameObject.

questions.question: Which window shows a list of all objects in the scene?
questions.explanation: The Hierarchy lists every GameObject present in the current scene.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Console window?
options: To display debug messages, warnings, and errors
questions.explanation: The Console shows output from Debug.Log, compilation errors, and runtime warnings.

questions.question: You can install multiple Unity Editor versions at the same time using Unity Hub.
questions.explanation: The Hub allows side-by-side installations of different Editor versions.

questions.question: The Library folder should be edited manually to speed up importing.
questions.explanation: The Library folder is auto-generated; modifying it can corrupt your project.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut focuses the Scene view on the selected object?
questions.explanation: Pressing F when an object is selected will frame it in the Scene view.

questions.question: How do you orbit the view in the Scene window?
questions.explanation: Holding Alt and dragging with the left mouse button orbits the view.

questions.question: What happens to changes made during Play mode after you exit?
options: They are only saved if you press Ctrl+S
They are applied to a copy of the scene
questions.explanation: All modifications made in Play mode are temporary and discarded upon stopping.

questions.question: The C# scripts, 3D models, and textures are stored inside the _____ folder.
questions.explanation: All user content goes into the Assets folder.

questions.question: What is an LTS release in Unity?
options: A Long Term Support version with extended stability
A version that requires a license
questions.explanation: LTS stands for Long Term Support and is recommended for production and learning.

questions.question: Which module is necessary for writing C# code in Unity?
questions.explanation: You need a code editor like Visual Studio to write and edit C# scripts.

questions.question: You can save a custom window layout for future use.
questions.explanation: Yes, use the Layout dropdown to save and load custom layouts.

questions.question: Which view shows exactly what the player will see?
questions.explanation: The Game view renders from the active camera, simulating the final player perspective.

questions.question: How do you fly through the Scene view like a first-person camera?
options: Hold right mouse button and use WASD
questions.explanation: Right-click and hold, then use WASD to move; hold Shift for faster speed.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using the Unity Hub?
options: It manages multiple Unity versions and projects
It builds the game for all platforms
questions.explanation: The Hub is a central launcher that organizes installations and projects.
